# Clunk

> Clunk is a quality gate for 3D assets. When an AI agent generates a GLB or glTF, the agent
> calls Clunk immediately and gets a policy verdict, a score, and a signed evidence record
> (Asset Passport) back before the asset moves downstream.
> 한국어: AI 에이전트가 3D 에셋을 만든 직후 스스로 호출하는 에셋 품질 게이트입니다.

Status: private pilot (Korea first). Billing is a working demo ledger, not a payment provider.

## What Clunk actually does

- Parses real GLB and glTF 2.0 bytes. No screenshot, no fixture, no mock metric.
- Records `inputHash` (SHA-256 of the input bytes), `coreBuildId`, `ruleSetId`, `ruleSetVersion`
  and `resultDigest` for every run.
- Evaluates 17 rules across 6 categories (format, scene, geometry, materials, textures, runtime).
  Rule set: `clunk-game-ready-v1` v`1.0.0`. Ready score threshold: 90.
- Every finding carries `ruleId`, `severity`, `path`, `observed` and `threshold`.
- Optimizes with an allowlist only, then re-inspects the produced artifact from scratch.

## Verdicts

- `준비 완료` (ready): no blocking finding, declared policy satisfied.
- `조건부 준비` (conditional): no hard blocker, warnings remain that lossless cleanup cannot fix.
- `차단됨` (blocked): at least one ERROR or CRITICAL finding remains.

## MCP server

Transport: stdio, JSON-RPC. `initialize` returns protocolVersion `2025-06-18` and
serverInfo `{ "name": "clunk", "version": "0.1.0" }`. Works with any MCP capable agent.

Client config:

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "clunk": {
      "command": "npm",
      "args": ["run", "mcp"],
      "cwd": "/path/to/clunk"
    }
  }
}
```

Tools returned by `tools/list`:

- `clunk_inspect` - Inspect a real GLB/GLTF using Clunk Core.
  input: `path` (required), `profile` (`web` | `mobile` | `pc`).
  output: inspection report, `inputHash`, `resultDigest`.
- `clunk_validate` - Validate a real GLB/GLTF against a declared policy.
  input: `path` (required), `profile`.
  output: `valid` boolean plus the same report.
- `clunk_optimize` - Apply only Clunk's allowlisted render-safe and metadata-only operations
  and write a new artifact.
  input: `path` (required), `outputPath`, `profile`.
  output: applied `operations`, `outputHash`, path of the new file.
- `clunk_passport` - Create a Passport by freshly inspecting source and output artifacts.
  input: `sourcePath` (required), `outputPath` (required), `profile`.
  output: Passport linking both hashes and both inspection digests.

Typical agent loop: `initialize` -> `tools/list` -> `clunk_inspect` -> (if fixable)
`clunk_optimize` -> `clunk_passport`.

## CLI

```bash
npm run clunk -- inspect <asset.glb> --profile pc
npm run clunk -- validate <asset.glb> --profile web
npm run clunk -- optimize <asset.glb> --out <output.glb>
npm run clunk -- passport <source.glb> <optimized.glb>
```

`validate` exits with code 2 when the asset does not satisfy the declared policy, so it can be
used directly as a CI gate. All commands print one JSON envelope on stdout.

Watch mode re-inspects files on change and keeps a bytes/sha256/score manifest fresh, with an
optional `--ref <commit>` stamp, so Clunk can sit inside a pipeline instead of being invoked
per event:

```bash
npm run clunk -- watch <paths...> --profile-file <profile.json> --manifest out.json --ref <commit>
```

## Texture set audit

Tiling/terrain textures intentionally live outside GLBs, so they get their own input type:
`scripts/texture-audit.mjs <config.json> [--strict]`. Per texture and usage density (m/tile) it
reports mip readability per camera-distance band (grade A-D with a numeric prescription), tile
seam verdicts (SEAMLESS / SOFT-SEAM / MASKED / VISIBLE-SEAM with placement-context exposure),
and mip-inclusive GPU memory versus a budget. `--strict` exits 2 on exposed seams, gameplay-band
D grades, or a blown budget (checks selectable via `strictChecks`). Calibrated against a real
game team's visual ground truth (8/8 agreement); see docs/texture-audit.ko.md.

## Safety boundaries

- The input file is never overwritten. Optimization always writes a separate artifact.
- Allowlisted operations only: `prune-empty-nodes`, `dedupe-materials`, `clean-metadata`,
  `repack`. The first, second and fourth are lossless; `clean-metadata` is metadata only.
- Not applied automatically in v1: mesh simplification, texture re-encoding, Draco or Meshopt
  compression, quantization, animation and skin edits, unknown extension rewrites.
- An asset is only reported ready after parse, policy, score, fresh re-inspection of the output
  bytes, blocker review, and reopening the downloaded artifact all pass.

## Local first

The web inspector parses asset bytes in the browser. Only metadata, hashes and results are
stored server side. Original asset bytes are not uploaded automatically, and artifact storage
is deliberately disabled during the pilot.

## Surfaces

Web inspector (`app/app`), CLI (`scripts/clunk-cli.ts`), MCP server (`integrations/mcp`),
VS Code extension (`integrations/vscode`). All four call the same Core contract and record the
same identifiers.

## Custom profiles

Project-specific inspection profiles are supported as JSON definitions: CLI `--profile-file <path.json>` and MCP tool argument `profileFile`. See docs/custom-profiles.ko.md and examples/profiles/harvest-frontier.example.json. Built-in profiles (web/mobile/pc) remain byte-identical. The web inspector accepts the same profile JSON for local-only inspection (no save, no credit).

## Generation pipeline

Agents can generate assets as procedural three.js factory code (img2threejs discipline,
Apache-2.0), extract a GLB with `scripts/threejs-to-glb.mjs <factory.mjs> <out.glb>`, and run it
through the normal gate (inspect -> optimize -> passport). Generation intelligence stays in the
agent; Clunk owns the rails and the gate. See docs/generate-pipeline.ko.md.

## Install (agents)

Clone https://github.com/Artemis-ignis/clunk , run `npm install`, then register the stdio
MCP server (`npm run mcp`, cwd = the clone) under the name "clunk". Verify readiness by
calling clunk_engine_profiles. The initialize response carries the recommended agent
workflow (ask for the user's engine, judge with enginePreset, fix-and-reinspect loop).
